compiled_state.title: As a developer, agent-side output truncation cannot mask diagnostics from the verifier
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Make the verifier immune to agent-side output filtering. Wrappers capture full output to artifacts before any pipe; the verifier reads only from artifacts, never from agent stdout. An agent invoking the wrapper with `2>&1 | tail -3` (or any other filter) cannot hide a lint/test failure from the verifier.

**Why**: SC2 — the user reporter's `dotnet test 2>&1 | tail -3` masking an IDE1006 lint diagnostic is a documented failure mode this story closes.

**Scope**:
- IN: wrapper output-capture happens before any output is returned to the agent's terminal; test fixtures verify the immunity end-to-end with real `tail`, `head`, and `grep -v` invocations.
- OUT: detection of truncation patterns in agent code (the design is immune by construction; pattern-detection would be belt-and-suspenders).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, an agent invoking `dso commit-step <name> 2>&1 | tail -3` (or `head -N`, `grep -v`, `>/dev/null`) does not change what the verifier sees in the artifact, and a hidden lint or test failure cannot slip through.
  ← Satisfies: "SC2 — Truncation-masking immunity"
- When this story is complete, end-to-end test fixtures exercise the wrapper with each truncating filter pattern documented in the user reporter's incident; each fails closed (verifier sees the failure).
  ← Satisfies: "SC2 — test fixture coverage"
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic.
  ← Satisfies: TDD Done-of-Done

## Considerations

- [Testing] Test fixtures must exercise real shell pipelines, not just unit-tested parser logic — the failure mode is the agent's invocation pattern, not the parser.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
